conflicts: Throat: Juki publishes no needle-to-arm figure for the F300. Dealer sheets (Juki Junkies, Premier Stitching) say 8.0 in and an Amazon bundle title says '9 inch Throat' (a seller's wording); Juki's brochure gives only 112 mm (4.5 in) underarm height and a 551 mm wide-table width. We list throat as [verify].
Knee lifter: one dealer lists it in the box, but Juki's F300 page and brochure list it as optional (standard on the F400 and F600).

Extension table and feet: Juki's F300 standard list has no wide table, walking foot or quilt foot; dealers and bundles (including Amazon's 'Quilters Package' listing B00F9K1FIM) add them, so bundle contents are the seller's.
Stitch count: Juki's page and brochure say 106; the 2009 manual (read by OCR, shared by the F600, F400 and F300) says 105 on its stitch-selection page. We use 106.
Weight: Juki says 21.6 lb; one dealer says 21 lb. We use Juki's figure.
Dimensions: height is 11.5 in on Juki's page and 29.1 cm (11.4 in) in the manual.
Price: Juki lists a $1,799 suggested retail price (F400 $1,999, F600 $2,369); our $799 is a Michaels sighting on 2026-09-29 and an eBay listing showed $699. Dealers set their own prices.
Ratings: Sewing Machines Plus shows 4.74 from 246 reviews; Amazon's single 'Quilters Package' bundle listing shows 4.2 from 40 ratings with no review text, and is not a rating of the base machine.

ownerThemes.theme: Owners single out the 16 sensor buttonholes as consistent and reliable, and describe the machine as very quiet.
A four-year owner still rates stitch quality as excellent; others report thick layers feeding well on the box feed.
PatternReview members comparing the F300, F400 and F600 note the F300 has the most favorable reviews of the three and ask what the extra stitches on the F600 actually buy.
QuiltingBoard members ask whether the F300 is enough machine for quilting or whether to stretch to the F600.

editorial.verdict: A 900 spm box-feed computerized machine with 106 stitches and 16 sensor buttonholes; Juki gives no throat figure, and the knee lifter, wide table and walking foot are extras.
editorial.whoFor: A sewer stepping up from a beginner machine who wants Juki's box feed and sensor buttonholes and does not need 225 stitches or the F600's bundled accessories.
editorial.skipIf: You need a published needle-to-arm figure for large quilts, or you want the knee lifter, walking foot and wide table included: Juki lists those as standard on the F600.
editorial.keySpec: 106 stitches · 900 spm · throat [verify] · box feed · 21.6 lb
strengths: Juki confirms 900 spm, a 7 mm width, a 5 mm length, box feed and the 130R / 705H needle system.
16 sensor buttonholes that PatternReview owners single out as consistent, in a machine they describe as quiet.
Owners report thick layers feeding well on the box feed, though a few report glitches on very heavy fabric.
weaknesses: The accessory set is thin: Juki lists the knee lifter, wide table, walking foot and quilt foot as not standard, and owners report buying them separately.
Juki publishes no throat figure; the 8 in on dealer sheets and the 9 in in one Amazon title are not Juki's, and Juki's only arm number is a 4.5 in underarm height.
Owner threads include breakage reports: a broken bobbin gear and a former owner calling it a lemon. Reddit skews toward help requests, so read these with care.

faqs.q: What is the price of the Juki HZL-F300?
faqs.a: Juki's suggested retail price is $1,799, and dealers set their own prices. Michaels showed $799 on 2026-09-29, so most buyers will see a figure well under list. Check what is in the box before comparing, since the walking foot, quilt foot, wide table and knee lifter are not standard.

faqs.q: How big is the throat on the Juki HZL-F300?
faqs.a: Juki publishes no needle-to-arm figure for the F300. Dealer sheets say 8 in and one Amazon bundle title says 9 in, neither from Juki, so we show throat as [verify]. Juki's brochure shows a 112 mm (4.5 in) underarm height and a 551 mm wide-table width, and neither is throat.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Juki HZL-F300 and HZL-F600?
faqs.a: Per Juki's pages and brochure, the F600 has 225 stitches and 4 fonts against 106 and 3 on the F300, and two LED lights against one. The F600 lists the walking foot, quilt foot, wide table and knee lifter as standard, while they are options on the F300. Juki lists $2,369 for the F600 and $1,799 for the F300.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Juki HZL-F300 and HZL-F400?
faqs.a: Juki lists the F400 with 157 stitches and 3 fonts against 106 and 3 on the F300. The walking foot, patchwork foot, quilt foot and knee lifter are standard on the F400, and the wide table is an option. Juki's suggested retail is $1,999 for the F400, $200 above the F300's $1,799.

faqs.q: Is the Juki HZL-F300 good for quilting?
faqs.a: Owners report thick layers feeding well on the box feed, with a few reporting glitches on very heavy fabric. Juki publishes no throat figure, and its standard list has no walking foot, quilt foot or wide table, so check arm space against your quilt size and price the extras. Dealer throat figures are not Juki numbers [verify].

faqs.q: What problems do owners report with the Juki HZL-F300?
faqs.a: Reliability and defects is a recurring owner theme: 13 of the 18 voices on it are negative, with reports such as a broken bobbin gear and one former owner calling the machine a lemon. Accessories are the other repeated complaint, as owners report buying the walking foot, quilt foot and table separately. Reddit leans toward people asking for help, so problems are over-represented.

faqs.q: How heavy is the Juki HZL-F300?
faqs.a: Juki gives 21.6 lb (9.8 kg), and one dealer says 21 lb. Juki's page lists 17.5 in wide, 11.5 in high and 8.25 in deep.

faqs.q: What bobbins and needles does the Juki HZL-F300 use?
faqs.a: Juki's page lists a class 15 bobbin and 130R / 705H needles with a low shank. The box holds 4 bobbins and a needle set.

faqs.q: Does the Juki HZL-F300 come with an extension table?
faqs.a: Not in Juki's standard list: the wide table is optional on the F300. One dealer says a table is included and bundle listings add one, so check the contents of the listing you buy.
